candidates.reason: The route, API contract, and authorized traffic describe a team invite-policy update that should be restricted to administrators.
candidates.broken_invariant: Only team administrators may change organization-level invite policy.
candidates.impact_rationale: A member-level policy change could weaken invite controls and alter team access governance.
candidates.repair_guidance: Enforce an administrator role check in the policy update handler or service before persisting invite-policy changes.
candidates.regression_test: Add a local non-destructive role-matrix test proving members cannot update invite policy while administrators can.
evidence_needed: Authorized local handler or service code showing where invite policy is persisted.
OpenAPI route metadata for the invite-policy update.
Redacted HAR route metadata showing the update route exists in authorized traffic.
false_positive_checks: Does a router dependency or middleware require an administrator role?
Is the policy scoped only to the caller's own preferences instead of team policy?
Does a downstream service reject non-admin role updates before persistence?
safe_validation_plan: Use local role fixtures or explicitly approved test accounts only.
Review role checks without changing live invite settings.
Keep the report draft submission-blocked until sanitized evidence is reviewed.

report_readiness.next_allowed_action: Review role-boundary evidence, refutation checks, repair guidance, and safety blockers before exporting a report preview.

required_items: Confirm the affected endpoint and code path using authorized local artifacts.
Resolve evidence gaps and false-positive checks before validation.
Complete redaction review before report export or sharing.

review_items: Confirm every candidate claim is traceable to imported authorized artifacts.
Review only normalized artifact summaries; raw paths, headers, tokens, and bodies remain excluded.
Compare endpoint, code path, invariant, and impact against prior submissions.
Treat similar scanner, dependency, fuzzing, or strategy signals as advisory until novelty is reviewed.

questions: Does an upstream middleware or policy layer already enforce the claimed boundary?
Can the affected endpoint and code path be reached under the authorized scope?
Does a local two-account or role-fixture check refute the suspected impact?

review_items: Confirm the candidate remains inside the imported policy and scope artifacts.
Check that the validation plan avoids prohibited actions before any execution.
Keep report submission blocked until policy, evidence, and redaction review are complete.
Confirm Scope Guard allows the exact asset, route, and validation mode.
Confirm validation remains non-destructive and uses only authorized test data.
Record human approval before executing any validation step.
